title: Maintain secrecy
author: Icy_Masterpiece_4414
selftext:
I’ve always been a paranoid, I remember years ago I was afraid of developers stealing my concept. Now thanks to AI, it happens at alarming rates. But for the longest time people used to say “it’s fine. ideas don’t matter, execution matters”

That was true solely because pre-AI no developer would blindly follow an idea because the work you needed to put behind it was too detrimental and could have easily failed.

Now everybody can execute. If it doesn’t work out then on to the next.

Now more than ever it’s the time to hold your secret. People ask me for screenshots of my project because they are interested and I have to refrain myself from showing it to the world.  
First the game is deployed, then you proceed to improve it. While they copy your already deployed game, you are improving said game, so they will always be behind.

Nowadays tons of people that use AI are looking at the business side of it. I will not lie, I’m kinda in for the same reason. Yes, of course there is passion too: only the code is written by AI, textures are all hand painted by me and models are paid from real artists. That’s how much I care.  
But since I’m in for the entrepreneurial side of it too, I have to think logically and from a marketing standpoint. 

Guys, these people will copy your game in less than a week, you have to be smart

comments.author: Mental_Tailor_4227
comments.body: I feel the same way. I’m currently working on a game that honestly have not shared with anyone. I know it will be a hit because it’s funny , cozy , cute and well added my own twist to your average rpg but easily able to be copied .

replies.body: It’s easy to copy because of AI, not because it can’t be a success. The concept is very … unique but easy, funny and witty implemented into “ not your average rpg/roguelike” but ez to copy. Theirs people that run 30-40 agents at a time copying games submitting them to Steam while people here are just trying to get players

comments.author: Ferniclestix
comments.body: eh if my game was shallow enough to be copied id worry about it.  I post about mechanics, how i built it  but nothing about the story, the quests, anything like that. to find that  out you have to play it when I release.  its a simple matter of been deeper than surface level guys.  if your game is that thin that a screenshot lets htem copy it then you gotta wonder.... ya know?

comments.body: I'd love to see someone copy mine 🤣

comments.author: selfish_meme
comments.body: Ideas don't matter because it's not easy to execute well and as soon as your app is out it's easy to replicate, better to get some enthusiasm going for it. Do the social media part well.

comments.author: LiquidZebra

comments.body: Let them steal it. If it works, you know it's legit. If it doesn't work, it's like them stealing your amazon package but only the box which you've prepared to throw out anyway.
